messages:
sara_billing: Heads up - nightly reconciliation showed ~31 invoices failed to link to NetSuite customers. net-sync-bot logged NS_ERR_NO_CUSTOMER_MATCH for external_customer_id values like 'acct_01Gx' vs expected 'cus_01Gx'. Seen since Stripe started sending new account-prefixed ids.

net-sync-bot: ns-import-20241012 failure: NS_ERR_NO_CUSTOMER_MATCH for invoices: inv_20241012_31..35. External customer ids: acct_01Gx, acct_01Gy. Mapping table lookup returned empty.

leo_backend: We rolled a change last week that switched to using Stripe's account-level customer id (acct_*) for some multi-tenant flows. Old exports used cus_*. Our NetSuite integration still maps on cus_* in external_id field. That mismatch causes import to not find customer records.

marta_accounting: Business impact: 31 invoices unposted in NetSuite, roughly $12.4k revenue pending. Customers were charged in Stripe. We need to ensure NetSuite records are linked before month close.

jules_pm: Which customers? Any enterprise accounts affected? Need to prioritize.

sara_billing: Sample impacted: Quasar Labs (acct_01Gx), PalletCo (acct_01Gy). Not enterprise contractually impacted but still high priority for AR. See sheet: https://redwood.internal/sheets/finance/stripe-acct-id-mismatch-20241012

leo_backend: Quick remediation options: 1) adapt import to treat acct_* as equivalent to cus_* by stripping acct_ prefix and trying fallback lookup, 2) backfill NetSuite mapping table to include acct_* forms for existing customers, 3) rollback change that started emitting acct_* in our Stripe exports. I can implement 1 quickly as a guard.

ops_bot: Who deployed the change and when?

leo_backend: Deploy 2024-10-05, PR #2102. It was intended to unify IDs across services but we missed NetSuite mapping consumer.

marta_accounting: Prefer option 2 (backfill mappings) plus 1 as temporary patch. Accounting needs deterministic mappings for audit. Backfilling maintains explicit trace.

leo_backend: Agreed. I'll push a hotfix that attempts fallback lookup (acct_* -> try cus_* by replacing prefix) and log all fallbacks. Then run a backfill to update mapping table with acct_* for existing customers. ETA hotfix 2h, backfill script 4h.

net-sync-bot: ns-import-20241012-backfill queued. Scanning invoices for NS_ERR_NO_CUSTOMER_MATCH...

net-sync-bot: backfill progress: 31 invoices processed -> 28 mapped via fallback patch, 3 still unmatched (customers missing external_id entirely). These 3 require manual NetSuite customer lookup.

marta_accounting: I'll manually reconcile the 3 with no external id and create mapping entries. Also will prepare AR notifications for affected customers.

sara_billing: Please ensure we create audit entries when we backfill mapping table so we can trace which ID variant was used. Also file an incident note for month close.

leo_backend: Added logging and an audit field in mapping table. PR #2147 created for fallback logic + backfill runner. Deployed hotfix; re-run import shows 28 previously failing invoices now posted.

ops_bot: Rolling window alert added: if >2% of invoices fail due to NO_CUSTOMER_MATCH escalate to on-call billing.

marta_accounting: Manual steps done for the 3 unmatched customers; posted invoices and reconciled AR. Total impact cleared. I'll update monthly close docs and send summary to finance leadership.

jules_pm: Thanks team. Action items: (1) permanent change: standardize exporter to emit cus_* again or update mapping consumers (decide by next week) (2) add automated test to catch id format drift (Leo) (3) incident report (Sara/Marta).

sara_billing: Will draft incident report and include customer communication if needed. Good catch. :thumbsup:
